dedupe_keys.name: sector readiness for climate change risks data centres techuk adaptation report 2021

description: This adaptation-planning case is the data-centre sector's report to the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs under the third round of the Adaptation Reporting Power, submitted by the trade body techUK in December 2021 and written by Emma Fryer. It set out the physical and non-physical climate risks to UK data centres, from flooding, identified as the most pressing, to heat, water stress, storms and effects on power and telecommunications supplies, and assessed how ready operators were, how they manage risk through site selection, redundancy and standards, and where adaptive capacity needed building. techUK followed it in January 2025 with Future-Proofing Digital Infrastructure: Climate Resilience in the Data Centre Sector, which added experience from the 2022 heatwave and transition risks from regulation and markets. Coverage: the United Kingdom's commercial data-centre sector, 2021 with an update in 2025. Format and access: free PDF reports on the techUK website. Caveats: an industry self-assessment based on member input, without site-level data; it is voluntary reporting. Simulation uses: climate adaptation planning of data-centre standards, hazard exposure screening of UK sites, and dependencies on energy and water in resilience models. Related records: the London heatwave outages tested these risks, XDI's analysis ranks global hubs, and the Ofcom and telecom adaptation reports cover networks.
